newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close lower on small NCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close lower on small NCD issue.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed slightly lower on Friday as the banking system's liquidity level remained stable following the central bank's relatively small issue of negotiable certificates of deposit, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 7.382 percent against Thursday's 7.418 close -- still outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was at 7.30-7.50 percent against 7.25-7.75.

The central bank issued T$3 billion in NCDs on Friday, one of its smallest issues in recent months and far below the double-digit issues of recent weeks, which were seen by brokers as aimed at cooling a red-hot stock market rally.
Taiwan's stock market saw its dramatic recent bull run halted by profit-taking on Friday, with the benchmark index falling 0.37 percent to 9,394.63.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield closed at 5.9650-9680 percent against 6.0000-0025.
